title: Wall Street ends lower as solid jobs data fuels hawkish Fed bets
summary:
How did August jobs report impact Fed rate expectations?
Labor market participation increased while the unemployment rate held firm at 4.1%.
"The labor market had a nice snapback last month, and ‌it's hard not to think an improving labor ⁠market is not a positive development for the economy," said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group in Omaha, Nebraska.
"On the flip side, the odds of a Fed hike increased a little bit as the economy ⁠continues to run a little on the hot side."
Financial markets are pricing in a 58.4% likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the conclusion of ​the ​Fed's September meeting, up from 49.4% on Thursday, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

title: Hiring blew past expectations in August, jobs report shows
summary:
The jobs report provided a gauge of the economy as the Fed weighs a rate hike.
Hiring grew far more than expected in August, bouncing back from a decline in employment a month earlier, according to the federal government's monthly jobs report.
Employers added 162,000 jobs in August, which marked a major improvement from 23,000 jobs lost in July, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed.
Employment surged in restaurants and bars, which added 59,000 jobs in August, after averaging just 12,000 jobs gained each month over the past year.
Central bankers, in turn, may examine the jobs report for information on the sturdiness of the labor market.

title: Trump keeps heralding an economic boom, but even a solid jobs report is causing problems for him
summary:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump has spent 20 months promising that America was on the cusp of an economic boom.
But speaking from the Oval Office, Trump instead launched into a grievance session about inflation and interest rates.
Stupidity causes inflation," Trump vented in the Oval Office, as he declared it "crazy" that the stock markets fell Friday on inflation concerns.
"When I win the election, we will immediately begin a brand new Trump economic boom," Trump said at an August 2024 rally in North Carolina.

title: US adds 162,000 jobs in August, raising Fed rate hike expectations
summary:

title: The Netherlands Shifted Billions in Gold Out of the US and Canada
summary:
London now holds 32.1% of the Netherlands' gold reserves, up from 18.1%, making it the largest overseas storage location for Dutch gold.
DNB sold about 59 tons of gold in New York and bought replacement bullion in London.
More than 27 tons were physically moved from the US and Canada to the Netherlands, while a similar amount was transferred from the Netherlands to London.
Germany and Italy, meanwhile, have faced political pressure to reconsider gold stored in New York, though neither central bank has announced plans to repatriate it.
A World Gold Council survey in June found 10% of central banks had diversified their overseas gold storage locations over the past year, up from 2% a year earlier.
